thread:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing GPU worker pods in us-west-2 failing kv-syncs and heavy retries. 50% increase in application retries since 08:12 UTC.

aj: saw that. Is it packet loss or latency? graphs show TCP retransmits on east-west hop between az-a and az-b.

lucas: looking at kube-proxy conntrack counters now — conntrack shows lots of TIME_WAIT and drops. could be hairpin/SNAT issue.

maria: I grabbed a tcpdump on pod -> service (ClusterIP) traffic. lots of RSTs and 1-2s TCP retransmits. dump: ```
08:14:32.123456 IP pod-a.svc.namespace > clusterip.svc.namespace: Flags [S], seq 0, win 29200
08:14:33.125678 IP pod-a.svc.namespace > clusterip.svc.namespace: Flags [S], seq 0, win 29200 (retransmit)
``` 
aj: paste of the netpol in that ns. it's a restrictive egress default-deny that we accidentally applied last week during tenant isolation rollout.

lucas: can you paste the NetworkPolicy YAML? suspect it's allowing pod CIDR but not service CIDR (clusterIPs).

maria: YAML snippet: ```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-egress-lockdown
  namespace: gpu-workloads
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.32.0.0/12   # pod CIDR range
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 2379
``` 
aj: yup — that ipBlock is pod CIDR only. clusterIPs are in 10.96.0.0/12. Pod->Service traffic to ClusterIP gets SNAT'd depending on kube-proxy rules and may use service CIDR. With this egress rule, clusterIP falls outside allowed egress so packets are dropped by CNI (calico).

lucas: additionally calico was enforcing policy with strict default deny. When pod hits clusterIP, two things can happen: hairpin to pod backend keeps source IP the pod's IP, but kube-proxy iptables mode might SNAT (MASQUERADE) for inter-node. If SNAT'd to node IP, that might fall outside the allowed ipBlock too.

maria: good catch. so the reason we saw increased conntrack and retransmits is that the egress rule was rejecting the clusterIP path, forcing retries and causing backpressure on gpu kv-sync.

aj: replication of problem: ran `kubectl exec` into failing pod and curl to service IP timed out. curl to podIP (direct) worked. So netpol is the culprit.

maria: proposed quick mitigation: add an egress rule to allow service CIDR and kube-apiserver/service cluster range. Command I used to test: ```
kubectl -n gpu-workloads patch networkpolicy tenant-egress-lockdown --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "add", "path": "/spec/egress/-", "value": {"to": [{"ipBlock": {"cidr":"10.96.0.0/12"}}] } } ]'
```
lucas: temporary allow looks good. We should instead update policy to allow namespaceSelector/podSelector based rules rather than relying on CIDR — more robust across clusters.

aj: raising point: some clusters have custom serviceCIDR — prefer policy: egress to namespaceSelector: {matchLabels:{kubernetes.io/metadata.name: "kube-system"}} and to podSelector: {} within same namespace for intra-namespace services. Example: ```
- to:
  - namespaceSelector: {}
    podSelector: {}
```  (that allows intra-namespace pod traffic to service backends without depending on CIDR)

maria: agreed. For now we rolled the quick patch at 08:22 UTC. metrics:
- retries back to baseline within 2 min
- tcp retransmits dropped ~85%
- kv-sync success rate returned to 99.6%

ops-bot: deploy-check: patch applied to NetworkPolicy/tenant-egress-lockdown in gpu-workloads by maria at 2026-03-18T08:22:11Z

jules: can we add an automation test to tenant policy rollout to validate clusterIP reachability to avoid regressing? maybe a simple curl job that hits internal services.

lucas: yes — add e2e check in the policy-rollout job: create an app with headless svc + ClusterIP and verify pod->svc curl. I'll open a PR.

maria: thx. follow-up actions:
- lucas: PR with namespace-selector-based policy (no CIDR hardcode)
- aj: checklist item to scan existing namespaces for netpols that allow podCIDR only
- jules: add policy-rollout e2e test

aj: FYI we'll also add a monitoring alert for sudden increase in inter-node TCP retransmit % so we can catch this earlier.

lucas: made issue infra/netpol-coverage-502

maria: :thumbsup: closing thread now — GPU job SLA restored. Will update postmortem with timeframe and mitigation steps.
